subsystems.name: Document ingestion and chunking
subsystems.role: turns source files into small 'text units' that extraction can cite back to.

subsystems.name: LLM extraction
subsystems.role: reads each chunk and pulls out entities, relationships and claims, with descriptions.

subsystems.name: Knowledge graph store
subsystems.role: holds the nodes and edges so relationships across documents survive.
parts: graph database (for example Neo4j or an in-memory graph)
vector index on entity and chunk embeddings

subsystems.name: Community detection and summarisation
subsystems.role: groups densely connected entities into hierarchical communities and writes a summary of each.

subsystems.name: Retrieval layer
subsystems.role: answers a query by choosing between global, local or hybrid search.
parts: global search: map-reduce over community summaries
local search: entity neighbourhood plus its source text units

subsystems.name: Generation and citation
subsystems.role: composes the final answer and links each claim back to source chunks.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the corpus
buildSteps.detail: Collect documents, parse them to plain text and split into overlapping chunks small enough for one LLM call each.

buildSteps.title: Extract a graph
buildSteps.detail: Send every chunk through an LLM that returns entities, relationships and claims as structured JSON; merge duplicates such as 'IBM' and 'International Business Machines'.

buildSteps.title: Build and store the graph
buildSteps.detail: Load nodes and edges into a graph database, attach the text-unit IDs that produced each one, and compute embeddings for entities and chunks.

buildSteps.title: Find communities
buildSteps.detail: Run hierarchical community detection (typically the Leiden algorithm) so the graph is partitioned from coarse top-level groups down to small clusters.

buildSteps.title: Summarise communities
buildSteps.detail: Ask the LLM to write a report on each community, from the leaves up, feeding child summaries into parent summaries to build a tree of global context.

buildSteps.title: Index for retrieval
buildSteps.detail: Store community reports, entity descriptions and chunk embeddings in indexes that support both graph traversal and vector similarity.

buildSteps.title: Answer a global question
buildSteps.detail: For 'what are the main themes?' run map-reduce: each relevant community report produces partial answers, which are reduced into one response.

buildSteps.title: Answer a local question
buildSteps.detail: For 'what did X say about Y?' start at the matched entities, walk their neighbourhood, pull the linked text units, and generate with citations.

buildSteps.title: Keep it fresh and evaluate it
buildSteps.detail: Add new documents incrementally, re-run extraction and affected summaries, and score answers against a held-out question set for faithfulness and coverage.

prerequisites.tech: Large language models capable of reliable structured extraction
prerequisites.why: the whole graph is built by asking a model to return entities and relationships as JSON.

prerequisites.tech: Graph databases with fast traversal and vector search
prerequisites.why: retrieval needs to hop between connected entities and also do similarity search.
provides the multi-level structure that makes global summarisation tractable.
indexing a corpus can mean one or more LLM calls per chunk, plus one per community, so cost is the main brake on adoption.
faithfulness, coverage and 'did it miss a theme?' are hard to measure, so improvements are hard to prove.

pathway.milestone: open-source GraphRAG pipelines and graph databases with built-in vector indexes
pathway.unlocks: teams can prototype global 'summarise this whole corpus' questions that plain vector RAG answers poorly.
living corpora — news, tickets, code — where re-indexing everything overnight is not acceptable.
graphs that merge the same entity across sources reliably, cutting duplicate nodes and wrong answers.

pathway.milestone: agentic retrieval that plans multi-hop queries and audits its own sources
pathway.unlocks: research and compliance work where the answer must come with a verifiable chain of evidence.
